title: DEIM-S vs DEIMv2-S: measured on the same protocol
dek: DEIMv2-S measures 0.9 mAP points higher than DEIM-S and uses less VRAM, but DEIM-S runs 37% faster on the same COCO protocol.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: DEIMv2-S is the more accurate model: 53.0 vs 52.1 mAP@50-95 on an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch, 0.9 points, and it uses less peak VRAM at 104 vs 142 MB. DEIM-S answers on speed, running 37% faster: 33.4 vs 24.3 FPS. The v2 revision trades throughput for accuracy and memory.
DEIMv2-S (released 2025-09-25) is the second-generation model; DEIM-S (2024-12-05) is the first. Both are Apache-2.0 and evaluated at 640 px, so the comparison isolates what the v2 revision changed.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. DEIM-S and DEIMv2-S highlighted against the full field.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent form. DEIMv2-S measures 53.0 mAP@50-95 to DEIM-S's 52.1, a 0.9 point gain. The two split on small objects, where DEIM-S leads 36.0 vs 35.0 mAP_small. Overall accuracy tilts to v2.

In PyTorch on the RTX 5070 Ti, DEIM-S runs 33.4 FPS to DEIMv2-S's 24.3, a 37% gap. The split holds under conversion: 97.6 vs 52.5 FPS on TensorRT FP32 and 82.4 vs 50.4 FPS on TensorRT FP16. On Jetson Orin, DEIM-S runs 10.2 FPS to DEIMv2-S's 5.7.

The pattern is consistent. DEIMv2-S leads on accuracy and DEIM-S on speed across 4 runtimes and 3 hardware platforms with verified data, down to the Raspberry Pi 5, where DEIM-S runs 1.1 FPS to DEIMv2-S's 0.8.

Pick DEIMv2-S when accuracy and memory matter more than frame rate: it is more accurate and uses less VRAM. Pick DEIM-S when throughput is the constraint, on GPU or on Jetson Orin, where it is faster by a wide margin. Both are Apache-2.0.

# pip install libreyolo
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO

deim = LibreYOLO("LibreDEIMs.pt")      # 10.32M params, 52.1 mAP@50-95
deimv2 = LibreYOLO("LibreDEIMv2s.pt")  # 9.78M params, 53.0 mAP@50-95

results = deimv2("image.jpg")
